subject: physics
question_text: Define amplitude, time period, frequency and phase of a particle in simple harmonic motion.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: Amplitude and time period
lines: the maximum displacement of the particle from
its mean position. SI unit: metre.
the time taken for one complete oscillation.
steps.why: Amplitude is measured from the MEAN position, not from one end of the path to the other — the end-to-end span is 2A, and one full oscillation covers a path of 4A.
common_mistakes: Calling the whole span of the motion the amplitude; that is twice the amplitude.

recall.must_convey: That amplitude is the maximum displacement from the mean position and the time period is the time for one complete oscillation.
accept: maximum displacement from the mean position

steps.label: Frequency and phase
lines: the number of oscillations made in one second.
the quantity (ωt + φ) that fixes where the
particle is and which way it is moving at that
steps.why: Phase is what separates two particles with the same amplitude and period but caught at different moments of their swing.
common_mistakes: Confusing phase with phase DIFFERENCE, which compares two oscillations rather than describing one.

recall.must_convey: That frequency is the number of oscillations per second, equal to one by T, and phase is omega t plus phi.
accept: phase is omega t plus phi
reject: maximum displacement from the mean position
